ai.description: *Indirana semipalmata* is a small frog (30–40 mm) with a brown, granular dorsum and a dark lateral band. It features partially webbed toes and a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana semipalmata* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, fleshy webbing that extends only to the base of the toes, unlike the more extensive webbing of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Indirana semipalmata* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and riparian zones of the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Brown Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its powerful hind legs to execute long, agile jumps to escape predators or navigate rocky stream environments.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana semipalmata* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 200–400 eggs on wet rocks near streams, where tadpoles develop in semi-aquatic, hygropetric conditions.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana semipalmata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting evergreen forests across Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at low to mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The *Indirana semipalmata* produces a series of short, high-pitched "ticking" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in Western Ghats rainforests.
